newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares hit eleventh record high.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares hit eleventh record high.

text.p: Demand for cement and milling shares powered Egyptian share prices to their eleventh record high on Sunday, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 8.43 points from Thursday to close at 380.61 points on turnover of 52.61 million pounds ($15.47 million).
"There is excess demand from everywhere. I honestly think a lot of people who have not previously entered the market are coming in," said broker Neveen al-Tahry of Delta EAB.
"The demand is unbelievable. Most of it seems to be going in two main directions - cement and flour mills," she said.

Five cement firms and three mills were among the top nine shares in terms of turnover. Amriyah Cement was the day's most active share, accounting for about 10.3 million pounds. Its share closed up 1.41 pounds at 86.4.

Helwan Portland Cement was the second most active share with 4.28 million pounds changing hands. Its share price was unchanged at 80 pounds. Suez Cement closed up .5 pounds at 72 in 3.48 million pounds worth of trade.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement fell 1.5 to close at 91 pounds, the CMA statement said.
Of the mills, North Cairo Flour Mills and Central and West Delta Flour Mills both were active with 3.1 million pounds and 2.8 million pounds in turnover respectively.
North Cairo closed up 9.4 at 206 pounds and West Delta rose 5.98 pounds to close at 125.62.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 620.66 from 603.3 points on Thursday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 254.65 from 249.99.
Out of the 84 shares traded, 53 gained, 11 lost and 20 ended the day unchanged.
